maria: Heads up — I'm planning to land a Terraform change that flips subnet route priority so dev VPCs prefer zonal NATs over the TGW attachment. Before I push, quick sanity check: could this blow up TGW route propagation or cause imports/plan surprises?

kevin: Which module/file are you touching?

maria: infra/networking/modules/egress/main.tf. PR here: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/4123

maria: snippet of the main change:
```hcl
resource "aws_route" "nat_pref" {
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.private.id
  destination_cidr_block = var.effective_cidr
  gateway_id             = aws_nat_gateway.this.id
  priority               = 100
}
```

maria: I'm adding lifecycle ignore_changes for tags and keeping the TGW route as fallback.

infra-bot: terraform plan started on workspace=dev-canary by maria (CI) :hourglass:

anna: Two quick things — 1) If any routes were created from the TGW attachment via propagation, TF might try to delete them unless you import the propagated routes into the module state. 2) Check any consumers that rely on TGW-specific next_hop IPs.

kevin: Can you run `terraform state list | grep aws_route` in the canary workspace and paste results? If there are aws_route resources already tied to TGW we should import rather than recreate.

maria: did a quick grep of state (canary):
```
aws_route.private["subnet-a"]
aws_route.private["legacy-tgw-route-subnet-b"]
```

maria: So there's one legacy tgw route. I'll import it with: `terraform import module.egress.aws_route.legacy_tgw_route \"rtb-xxx_0.0.0.0/0\"` — correct?

kevin: Import format usually `terraform import module.egress.aws_route.legacy_tgw_route rtb-xxxxx_0.0.0.0/0` yes. After import run plan to ensure no diffs.

sam: Also double-check NAT EIP rotation secret wiring — we had a bug last quarter where tfvars with eip ids were checked in. Make sure the people running apply have Vault access to `secret/infra/nat-eips`.

jen: FYI the secrets path is `secret/infra/nat-eips` (managed by ops). I added short docs in the runbook: https://wiki.internal/rw/infra/nat-rotation. No plaintext EIPs in repo.

maria: thanks — I'll import then run plan and paste the plan output here. Intend to do a canary apply in dev-canary tomorrow 09:30 PT if green.

kevin: I can run the canary apply. Ping me 10m before.

maria: pinging @kevin — will DM 10m before.

infra-bot: terraform plan finished with 1 change to be applied in workspace=dev-canary (apply pending).

kevin: Quick review — minor docs nit but the code change LGTM from infra perspective. Two asks: add a comment about why priority=100 and add an owner tag on the route resource.

maria: will add both. Also added `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [tags] }` to avoid churn from tag updates by allocator.

maria: merging after CI; schedule apply for 09:30 PT tomorrow in canary. Anyone object?

anna: no objections. please coordinate with network on-call if anything unexpected.

jen: reminder — after apply, run the e2e DNS smoke test in the runbook (k8s -> external service). Link is in the runbook.

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll run apply and the smoke test, and post results here.

maria: thanks all, merging now.

infra-bot: PR merged by maria — CI pipeline started (checks: plan, fmt, unit-tests).

maria: ci is green, will DM kevin 10m before apply tomorrow.

kevin: great, thanks.

maria: (post-apply) applied in dev-canary at 09:31 PT, no errors. E2E DNS smoke test passed. Noted one extra propagated route remained and was left as fallback per lifecycle config.

kevin: thanks for running it. I'll schedule the prod rollout after we validate across two more canaries.

maria: filed follow-up ticket to sweep legacy TGW routes and document import steps: https://issues.internal/INFRA-2781

jen: good runbook updates, thanks.

maria: closing the loop — leaving this thread for record.
